title: How would you design a social feed / timeline at scale (e.g. Instagram/Twitter): fanout-on-write (push a fully denormalized post entry into each follower's precomputed timeline so reads are an O(1) list lookup) vs fanout-on-read (pull + merge at read time), and why do you use a HYBRID (fanout-on-write for normal users, fanout-on-read for celebrities with millions of followers to avoid massive write amplification)?
shortTitle: How would you design a social feed / timeline at scale
keyPoints: Fanout-on-write precomputes each follower's timeline for O(1) reads but amplifies writes by follower count.
Fanout-on-read stores posts once and assembles the feed at read time; cheap writes but expensive reads.
Neither pure strategy works: celebrity posts would trigger millions of writes, and pull on every read is too slow.
The hybrid uses fanout-on-write for normal users and fanout-on-read for celebrities above a follower threshold.
Cache celebrity posts aggressively since many followers pull the same ones; cap timeline size to bound storage.
Do the write fanout asynchronously through a queue so posting returns immediately.
The celebrity threshold is the knob that trades write cost against read cost.

s1_definition.oneliner: Fanout-on-write precomputes timelines for O(1) reads but amplifies writes by follower count, fanout-on-read keeps writes cheap but makes reads expensive, and the hybrid uses fanout-on-write for normal users and fanout-on-read for celebrities to avoid writing to millions of timelines per post.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Fanout-on-write (push)** – On post, push a denormalized entry into each follower's precomputed timeline; read is a simple list lookup.
- **Fanout-on-read (pull)** – Store posts once; on read, pull and merge the followees' recent posts; writes are trivial.
- **Write amplification** – One post triggers N writes where N is the follower count; catastrophic for celebrities.
- **Hybrid** – Fanout-on-write for normal users (modest followers), fanout-on-read for celebrities (millions of followers).
- **Celebrity threshold** – The follower count above which a user is treated as a celebrity; trades write cost vs read cost.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India sending account-activity notices. Fanout-on-write stuffs a copy into every interested customer's mailbox immediately, so opening the mailbox is instant, but one event for a million customers means stuffing a million mailboxes. Fanout-on-read keeps one noticeboard and gathers relevant notices on demand, which is cheap to post but slow to read. The hybrid: stuff mailboxes for ordinary notices, and for notices that interest millions, fetch on demand and blend in.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Hybrid Feed Design:

  Normal User Posts (PUSH):
  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
  │ analyst-     │───▶│ Queue    │───▶│ Worker   │───▶│ Timeline │
  │ pankaj posts │    │ (async)  │    │ (fanout) │    │ follower │
  │              │    └──────────┘    │ to 500   │    │ mailboxes│
  └──────────────┘                    │ timelines│    └──────────┘
                                      └──────────┘

  Celebrity Posts (PULL at read):
  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐
  │ market-index │───▶│ Post     │  (1 write, no fanout)
  │ posts        │    │ Store    │
  └──────────────┘    └─────┬────┘
                            │ on read
  ┌──────────────┐          │
  │ Rajesh reads │          │
  │ feed         │          │
  └──────┬───────┘          │
         │                  │
  ┌──────▼──────────────────▼──────┐
  │ Merge:                        │
  │   Precomputed timeline        │
  │   + Cached celebrity posts    │
  │   -> Sorted by time           │
  └───────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A social feed at scale is a trade-off about where you pay the cost. Fanout-on-write precomputes timelines for instant reads but triggers N writes per post where N is the follower count. Fanout-on-read stores posts once but makes every read an expensive multi-account merge. Neither pure strategy works because the follower distribution is extremely skewed: most users have few followers but some have millions.

The hybrid resolves this by choosing the strategy per author. Normal users get push: their posts are written into followers' timelines for instant reads. Celebrities get pull: their posts are stored once and merged at read time from a cache. Rajesh's feed reads his precomputed timeline plus a few cached celebrity pulls.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj built an investor-updates feed this way. Analysts with modest followings were fanned out on write. A market-index account with millions of followers was pulled at read time. The celebrity threshold, set from the real follower distribution, is the knob that trades write cost against read cost.

Remember one sentence: use fanout-on-write for normal users so reads are instant, and fanout-on-read for celebrities so one post never triggers millions of writes, giving a hybrid that pays the cost where it is cheapest for each class of user.
